title: Customer Show + Tell: How Cynet Replaced Manual Demo Building and Reporting With the Navattic MCP
summary: Cynet uses Navattic’s MCP to automate demo reporting, give every launch an interactive tour, and run webinars that show who engaged.
body_markdown:
Every product marketer has a demo horror story. A data center goes down mid-conference. A keynote demo fails in front of 3,500 people. PowerPoint crashes halfway through a webinar.


Matt Duench, who leads product marketing at Cynet, has lived some version of all three. At our Toronto Fanattic event, he walked through how his team now uses Navattic across three use cases: MCP-powered reporting and demo building, interactive product launches, and live presentations that replace static decks.


Highlights & results


- **Reporting in one question:** A Teams agent connected to the Navattic MCP returns top demos, engagement, insights, and charts on demand, replacing copy-and-paste reports
- **Demos built from a text prompt:** The team is starting to build demos through the MCP by describing what they need
- **Every launch gets a tour:** Every product launch, product, and solution area at Cynet now gets its own Navattic demo
- **Live presentations with real engagement data:** Cynet ran its monthly Last Call threat intelligence webinar entirely in Navattic and could see who viewed, clicked, and spent time on what


The challenge: static content, untrackable engagement


Cynet manages attack paths with AI across identity, endpoint, SaaS, and cloud. Matt's team had three problems to solve:


- **Static presentations:** Decks and webinars meant one person standing in front of slides. Low engagement, and no way to see who actually paid attention. Shared registration links made attendee data unreliable.
- **A product that's hard to explore before talking to sales:** Most security sites push visitors straight to "book a demo." Matt wanted buyers to choose their own path through the product first, so they show up to sales already warmed up.
- **Manual reporting:** Pulling demo data meant copying and pasting into slides for executives.


Matt brought a principle from his time at Okta: show, don't tell.


> "We don't wanna be tell, tell, tell. It's let's show you how the product works. Let's personalize it in such a way that we can show you the solution along your buyer journey that matches your use case."


Where Navattic fits: MCP-powered reporting, launches, and live presentations


### MCP-powered reporting and demo building


Reporting used to be the most manual part of Matt's job.


> "The data analysis, it used to be really super time consuming, hugely manual. Really challenging to get the data out, challenging to report to the business."


Cynet runs on Microsoft Teams, so Matt built a Teams agent called Jordan and connected it to the Navattic MCP. Jordan also draws on Cynet's marketing brain for market and competitive intelligence.


Getting answers now takes one question:


> "I can say, hey, Jordan, tell me my top five Navattic demos over the last thirty days. What's the engagement? What are some interesting insights? And it'll come back with some insights and even produce some really nice graphs."


Matt also uses the MCP to schedule weekly reports that show which demos get the most engagement and where his team should spend time improving them.


**Building demos from a text prompt**


His team is also starting to build demos through the MCP. Matt describes the demo he wants, and the MCP pulls the right captures and flows in Navattic.


> "Let's build Matt's awesome demonstration, just in text, with the MCP, and it being able to do that in Navattic, pulling the captures that I tell it, pulling the flows that I tell it. Pretty empowering, pretty encouraging."


Matt is early in his MCP rollout, but it's been easy to pick up and iterate on.


> "I have yet to stump these tools. I've yet to give it a question, a use case that it can't solve or at least get down a path where I can iterate and build with it. And Navattic is very much like that."


### Interactive product launches


Every Cynet launch now ships with a Navattic tour. Buyers can step through what's new or skip straight to the parts they care about.


> "You can almost choose your own adventure, where if I don't wanna go through the whole demonstration, I don't have to. I can select what's interesting to me."


Matt also made it a rule on his team: every product and solution area gets its own demo. It's step one in building out a full demo library.


### Live presentations


Cynet's innovation lab, Cynet Labs, is experimenting with a faster way to build presentations:


1. Build an animation in an AI tool like Claude
2. Export it as HTML
3. Capture it in Navattic and turn a static presentation into an interactive one in seconds


Matt's team recently ran its monthly Last Call threat intelligence webinar entirely in Navattic. That solved the tracking problem too.


> "I can share that link now for my webinar effectively, and I know who's viewed what. I know who spent time on what, who's clicked what."


Presentation mode helps here. When one of Matt's UK SEs asked how to see the product without the tooltips and modals in the way, Matt showed him the presentation mode shortcut. The guidance disappeared, and the SE could demo the product live from the same tour.


The results: early wins across the team


Matt was upfront that it's early, but the response inside Cynet has been strong:


- **Reporting without the busywork:** Weekly demo reports and on-demand insights replaced copy-and-paste updates for executives
- **Faster demo builds:** The MCP pulls captures and flows from a text prompt
- **Live presentations with real engagement data:** Webinars and launches now show who engaged and with what
- **Leadership is bought in:** After seeing the interactive webinar, Cynet's CMO asked, "What can't Navattic do?"


> "I'm encouraged by the capabilities of the MCP and being able to more dynamically get that intelligence back. It's been a huge win for our team."


What's next: Gong-triggered personalized demos


Cynet just onboarded Gong and Clay. Matt's next build connects them to Navattic:


1. A keyword in a Gong call, like "identity security," triggers a workflow
2. Clay enriches the account and finds other stakeholders who should see the demo
3. The Navattic MCP and brain build a personalized demo
4. HubSpot sends it to each stakeholder


Cynet also sells through managed service providers (MSPs). Matt is exploring Launchpad to help MSPs share Cynet's existing demos with their own clients.


Key takeaways


- **Let an agent handle demo reporting.** Connect the Navattic MCP to the tools your team already uses, and ask for engagement insights instead of pulling them by hand.
- **Build demos by describing them.** The MCP can pull the captures and flows you name, so a first draft starts from a prompt.
- **Give every launch a tour.** Let buyers choose what to explore instead of sitting through the full story.
- **Make presentations trackable.** A webinar delivered as an interactive demo tells you who engaged and with what.
- **Experiment.** In Matt's words, the only limit is your own creativity.
